context: Mari and Barton are comrades exploring a lower level; Mari—who knows her way around locks and was responsible for this door—finds it ajar and insists she didn't unlock it. Barton is more easygoing and offers practical, dismissive explanations: maybe the ancient door failed, someone else opened it, or they just got lucky. Off-screen possibilities to consider (from related scenes) include another person or guard having been persuaded to open the entrance, the door having been tampered with or broken, or it simply being unlocked before their shift. Their exchange is a cautious debate over those possibilities, with Mari suspicious and Barton brushing off her concerns.
